verdict: Revenue grew 6% to $1.09B — a 100th straight quarter of growth — but profit fell 3% because insurance and claims costs jumped and winning new residential customers got harder.

kpis.label: Operating income
kpis.note: Margin 20.5%, down from 21.9% a year ago

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: +28.8% YoY, helped by a $63M tax refund

segments.note: Franchise royalties and other small income

takeaways.title: Sales still growing
takeaways.text: Revenue hit $1.09B, the 100th quarter in a row of growth. Commercial work grew fastest at +7.7%, while residential grew +4.9%.

takeaways.title: Insurance costs squeezed profit
takeaways.text: Net income fell to $158M. Insurance and claims costs roughly doubled to about $37M across service and office costs, and management called residential customer sign-ups disappointing.

takeaways.title: Cash flow was strong
takeaways.text: Free cash flow (cash left after running costs and small investments) rose 29% to $235M, and Rollins spent $120M buying back its own shares.

oneTimers: Acquisition-related charges of $8M (intangible amortization and revaluing earn-out promises from the Fox, Saela and Romex deals) are excluded from the company's adjusted profit.
Operating cash flow included a $63M tax refund tied to a tax-credit strategy, which flattered the free-cash-flow growth rate.
